title: Ajay Devgn Just Dropped the Son of Sardaar 2 Trailer. He Did It While His Other Film Was Smashing the Box Office.
excerpt: Jassi is back — this time in Scotland, with Mrunal Thakur, a dead man's final performance, and enough Punjabi swagger to fuel a whole summer. Meanwhile, Dhamaal 4 crossed ₹35 crore in two days.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ajay Devgn released the *Son of Sardaar 2* trailer while *Dhamaal 4* is performing well at the box office.
  • The sequel features Mrunal Thakur and a mix of Punjabi and Scottish themes.
  • Mukul Dev's final performance adds emotional depth to *Son of Sardaar 2*.
  • Dhamaal 4 recorded ₹36 crore in two days, aiming for a ₹65 crore opening weekend.
  • The film targets global Indian audiences with its Scotland setting.
Star-Studded Cast
›Mrunal Thakur joins Ajay Devgn as the new lead.
›Mukul Dev's last performance adds emotional weight.
›Supporting cast includes Ravi Kishan, Deepak Dobriyal, and more.
›Film features a mix of comedy and action.

There is a particular kind of Bollywood dominance that involves not just having a hit — but having a hit *and* casually dropping the trailer for your next film while the numbers are still climbing. Ajay Devgn did exactly that on Friday, unveiling the *Son of Sardaar 2* trailer at a grand event in Mumbai while Dhamaal 4 was busy crossing half a million tickets on BookMyShow.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=HSX_KPfbP1o

The man is having a weekend.

![Mrunal Thakur — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/78/Mrunal_Thakur_in_Andheri_1_%28cropped%29.jpg)

Jassi Returns — With a Passport

The trailer opens with a wink to the original: "2012, he survived Punjab. Now will he survive Scotland?" And just like that, we're back in the world of Jassi — the lovable, turbaned troublemaker who turned the 2012 original into a ₹100 crore hit. This time, the chaos has gone international.

> "Now will he survive Scotland?" And just like that, we're back in the world of Jassi — the lovable, turbaned troublemaker who turned the 2012 original into a ₹100 crore hit."

Mrunal Thakur steps in as the new leading lady in her first on-screen pairing with Devgn, and the chemistry feels distinctly different from the original's Sonakshi Sinha dynamic. Where the first film leaned into desi earthiness, the sequel swings between Punjabi swagger and Scottish highlands with the confidence of a man who's done this before.

The nearly three-minute trailer is a sensory assault in the best possible way: a wedding that goes spectacularly wrong, Devgn's signature split-between-two-cars entry (yes, again — and honestly, we'd be disappointed if it weren't there), and a *Border* reference that lands like an inside joke between Ajay and every Indian who grew up in the '90s.

The Supporting Cast Is Stacked

![Ravi Kishan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8d/Ravi_Kissen_at_the_launch_of_T_P_Aggarwal%27s_trade_magazine_%27Blockbuster%27_20.jpg)

The film reunites a murderer's row of comic talent. Ravi Kishan, fresh off a scene-stealing turn in Dhamaal 4, shows up here too. Deepak Dobriyal — who can make a grocery list sound funny — is in. Chunky Panday, Sanjay Mishra, Vindu Dara Singh, Kubbra Sait, and Neeru Bajwa round out a cast that reads like a fantasy draft for a Bollywood comedy league.

But the name that carries the most weight is Mukul Dev.

The actor, who played the iconic villain Tony in the original *Son of Sardaar*, passed away earlier this year. This is his last film. The trailer doesn't make a spectacle of it — his scenes are woven naturally into the fabric of the story — but the knowledge that this is the final time audiences will see him on screen gives the film a layer of emotion its genre doesn't usually carry.

> "Action! Emotions! Confusion ka bhandaar. JASSI is back, aur iss baar sab kuch double hai!" — Ajay Devgn, sharing the trailer on Instagram

The Context Makes It Bigger

Here is what makes this trailer drop genuinely remarkable: it arrived on the same day Dhamaal 4 recorded a 61% surge on its second day, tracking an estimated ₹23.5 crore on Saturday alone. The two-day total now sits around ₹36 crore, with the film on pace for a ₹65 crore opening weekend — outperforming *Welcome to the Jungle* at the same stage.

Ajay Devgn is now running two franchise machines simultaneously. Dhamaal 4 is the seventh-biggest Bollywood opening day of 2026. Son of Sardaar 2 arrives in theatres on July 25, barely two weeks away. In an industry where stars carefully space their releases to avoid cannibalizing each other, Devgn is essentially competing with himself — and winning both sides of the fight.

The film is directed by Vijay Kumar Arora and produced under Devgn Films alongside Jio Studios and YRV Studios, with Jyoti Deshpande co-producing.

For the Diaspora

The Scotland setting is a deliberate nod to the global Indian audience — a location that UK-based NRIs know intimately and one that American desis associate with epic Bollywood set pieces (every *DDLJ* pilgrimage through Europe started somewhere). With Devgn's overseas numbers already looking strong — Dhamaal 4 outperformed both *Cocktail 2* and *Welcome to the Jungle* in Australia and New Zealand on Day 1 — the franchise clearly has diaspora appeal baked in.

*Son of Sardaar 2* releases in cinemas on July 25, 2026. The original grossed over ₹100 crore in 2012. If the trailer is any indication, Jassi has unfinished business — and this time, he's brought his passport.
